predecessors.name: Ottoman Empire
predecessors.text: the Ottoman vilayets of the Syrian interior, entered by the Arab forces on 1 October 1918; the page names the preceding entity as OETA East without a start date

successors.name: French Mandate for Syria and the Lebanon
successors.text: Damascus and Syria, which 'surrendered to French forces on 25 July 1920'; General Gouraud divided the French mandate territory into several smaller states on 1 September 1920

successors.name: Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan
successors.text: Transjordan, which became 'for a short time, a no man's land' after the Battle of Maysalun (July 1920) until Abdullah's Emirate of Transjordan of April 1921

ledger.x: 5 October 1918: Faisal announces an Arab government at Damascus.
8 March 1920: the Emirate is proclaimed a kingdom with Faisal I as king and Hashim al-Atassi as prime minister.
24 July 1920: the French invade after the ultimatum of 14 July.
ledger.cpn: French Mandate for Syria and the Lebanon

ledger.x: 25 July 1920: the fighting ends with the surrender of Damascus to French forces.
ledger.cpn: French Mandate for Syria and the Lebanon

ledger.x: 25 July 1920: Damascus falls and the kingdom ends.
ledger.cpn: French Mandate for Syria and the Lebanon

wars.name: Franco-Syrian War
wars.outcome: The French defeated the Syrian army at Maysalun on 24 July 1920 and took Damascus on 25 July; Faisal was expelled in August.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line; the Damascus Program of July 1919 states claims, the Franco-Syrian frontier at the coast is not on the page.
